risks: Quoted shares of Jayabharat Credit Limited were thinly traded on the stock exchange and the company would not be able to execute the large volume at quoted price on the Stock Exchange.
The Board of Directors has constituted Risk Management Committee (RMC) to implement and monitor the risk management plan of the Company
The company pursues a comprehensive Risk Management Programme as an essential element of sound corporate governance and it is committed to continuously embedding risk management in its daily culture
Each identified risk is assessed according to its probability and impact on the company
The Board of Directors has formed an Internal Risk Management Committee to identify, evaluate, mitigate and monitor the risk management in the company
Business risk evaluation and management is an ongoing process within the company. The assessment is periodically reviewed by the Board.

Risk in literal terms can be defined as the effect of uncertainty on the objectives. Risk is measured in terms of consequences and likelihood. Risks can be internal and external and are inherent in all administrative and business activities.
Factors like changes in Government regulations, tax laws and other factors such as industrial relations and economic developments, etc may further influence in company's operations or performance.
Impairment of financial assets based on assumptions about risk of default and expected loss rates
Fair value measurement of financial instruments using valuation techniques with unobservable inputs
Recoverability of advances/receivables requiring significant management judgement
Uncertainties in interpretation of complex tax regulations and changes in tax laws
Provisions and contingencies where outcome of pending matters cannot be predicted with accuracy
Defined benefit obligation estimates sensitive to assumptions on inflation, mortality, discount rate, and salary increases
Salary Risk: Deviation in rate of increase of salary in future for plan participants from the rate used to determine present value of obligation will have a bearing on the plan's liability.
Investment Risk: If plan liability is funded and return on plan assets is below Government Bonds Yield, it will create a plan deficit.
Interest Risk (Discount Rate risk): A decrease in the bond interest rate (discount rate) will increase the plan liability.
Mortality Risk: A change in mortality rate will have a bearing on the plan's liability.
Price risk due to investments in equity shares and mutual funds
Interest rate risk due to term deposits with banks and long-term debt obligations with floating interest rates
Credit risk from trade receivables, deposits with banks, and cash equivalents

Variation in assumptions for defined benefit obligation (inflation, medical cost trends, mortality, discount rate, salary increases)
